sentences.text:
Through: Mr.Jyoti Mehra and Mr.
 Sharma, Advocates
 versus
 State And Ors. 
 Through: Mr.Sunil Kumar Gautam,
 State with Si Rav
 R2 in person for 
 No.3 to 5.

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Yogesh Khanna

Petitioner files this petition for quashing of the FIR No.320/2019 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Kalkaji, Delhi against respondents No.2 to 5 and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner/complainant and respondent No.2 was solemnized on 02.07.2007 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
From this wedlock boy Akshaj Lal and girl Amaira were born on 11.05.2008 and 20.03.2015 respectively.

Due to matrimonial discord,
the couple could not live together and on the complaint of petitioner aforesaid FIR was registered against the respondents No.2 to 5.
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple has settled the matter per Memorandum of Understanding dated 11.11.2022.
Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner has joined the matrimonial home with respondent No.2 and both of them are living happily and peacefully.
The petitioner does not wish to take any further action against respondents No.2 to 5 and pendency of proceedings will certainly be hurdle in her matrimonial life.
3. The complainant/petitioner has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the respondents No.2 to 5 and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

4. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as petitioner /complainant has settled all the disputes and joined the matrimonial home with respondent No.2.
Both of them are living happily.

In view of the above, there is no use to continue Smt Geetika Lall vs State And Ors on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49045734/
1 with the proceedings against respondents No.2 to 5 it would never entail in their conviction.

No order as to costs.
